'''Roger Parsons''' {{postnominals|country=GBR|size=100%|FRSC|FRS}} (1926 {{endash}} 7 January 2017) was a British [[chemist]] ([[electrochemist]]).<ref>{{cite web| first=Roger| last=Alder |url=http://www.bristol.ac.uk/news/2017/february/professor-roger-parsons-1927-2017.html |title=Professor Roger Parsons, 1927–2017 | publisher=[[University of Bristol]] |date=6 February 2017 |access-date=21 February 2017}}</ref>

==Biography==

Parsons studied chemistry at [[Imperial College London]], obtaining a first class bachelor's degree in 1947. His doctorate, supervised by [[John Bockris]], was awarded the following year. In 1951 he was appointed lecturer at the University of St. Andrews in Dundee (now [[Dundee University]]), researching [[electrochemical kinetics]] and thermodynamics under [[Douglas Hugh Everett]]. In 1954, Parsons accompanied Everett to the [[University of Bristol]], where he was appointed professor. In 1977 Parsons was appointed Directeur du Laboratoired'Electrochimie Interfaciale (director of the laboratory of interfacial electrochemistry) at the [[CNRS]] in France, moving to [[Southampton University|Southampton]] in 1985 before retiring in 1992.<ref name="Hillman">{{cite journal| title=Professor Roger Parsons F.R.S.C., F.R.S.| url=http://www.ise-online.org/ise-about/files/Parsons_CV.pdf| first=Robert| last=Hillman| journal=Journal of the Chemical Society, Faraday Transactions| publisher=[[Royal Society of Chemistry]]| volume=92| issue=20| year=1996| issn=0956-5000| doi=10.1039/ft99692fp205| page=205| archive-date=11 June 2017| access-date=26 August 2018| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170611151716/http://ise-online.org/ise-about/files/Parsons_CV.pdf| url-status=live}}</ref>

Parsons served as editor of the ''[[Journal of Electroanalytical Chemistry]]'' and as president of the Faraday Division of the [[Royal Chemical Society]].<ref name="Hillman"/>

==Research==

His work dealt with kinetics (especially hydrogen evolution in electrolysis), [[electrocapillarity]] and adsorption processes, optical methods in interfacial electrochemistry, single crystal electrode processes and the [[Double layer (surface science)|electrochemical double layer]].<ref name="Hillman"/>

==Awards and honours==

In 1979, he was awarded the [[Olin Palladium Award]] by the [[Electrochemical Society]].<ref name="ECS">{{cite web | title=Olin Palladium Award | website=ECS | date=26 August 2018 | url=https://www.electrochem.org/palladium-award | access-date=26 August 2018 | archive-date=7 May 2018 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180507003643/https://www.electrochem.org/palladium-award | url-status=live }}</ref> Parsons was elected to the [[Royal Society]] in 1980,<ref name="RS">{{cite web | title=Roger Parsons | website=Royal Society | date=12 August 2015 | url=https://royalsociety.org/people/roger-parsons-12043/ | access-date=26 August 2018 | archive-date=26 August 2018 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180826214541/https://royalsociety.org/people/roger-parsons-12043/ | url-status=live }}</ref> and won the society's [[Davy Medal]] in 2003.<ref name="Davy">{{cite web | title=Davy Medal | website=Royal Society | date=10 July 2018 | url=https://royalsociety.org/grants-schemes-awards/awards/davy-medal/ | access-date=26 August 2018 | archive-date=26 September 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150926175111/https://royalsociety.org/grants-schemes-awards/awards/davy-medal/ | url-status=live }}</ref>
